name: 2Africa Submarine Cable System
operator: 2Africa Consortium (Meta, China Mobile, MTN, Orange, Telecom Egypt, Vodafone, WIOCC)
famous_for: Longest subsea cable system ever built, circling the African continent across 45,000 km to Europe and Asia
story: 2Africa is the longest subsea cable system in history, measuring over 45,000 kilometers and encircling the entire continent of Africa while providing direct links to Southern Europe, the Middle East, and South Asia. Backed by Meta, China Mobile International, MTN GlobalConnect, Orange, Telecom Egypt, Vodafone, and WIOCC, the system employs 16-pair SDM technology delivering up to 180 Tbps of nominal capacity. Landings span 46 locations across 33 nations, connecting hundreds of millions of people to high-capacity international Internet transit.
notable: Extends over 45,000 kilometers connecting 33 countries across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and South Asia.
Designed with nominal capacity of up to 180 Tbps using 16 fiber pair space-division multiplexing.
Funded by a global consortium led by Meta alongside African, European, and Asian telecom carriers.
Includes the 2Africa Pearls extension connecting the Persian Gulf, Pakistan, and Mumbai.

name: Akamai Intelligent Edge Platform
famous_for: World's most distributed edge and cybersecurity mesh spanning 4,000+ locations across 130+ countries
story: Founded in 1998 by MIT mathematician Tom Leighton and Danny Lewin, Akamai established the modern Content Delivery Network (CDN) industry. Operating more than 350,000 edge servers deployed deep inside thousands of ISP networks worldwide, Akamai's core backbone interconnects regional mega-clearinghouses and scrubbing centers across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and Africa. The platform delivers upwards of 100 terabits per second of daily peak web traffic while mitigating massive distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks globally.
notable: Pioneered edge computing and distributed content delivery algorithms created at MIT in 1998.
Deploys over 350,000 servers in approximately 4,000 locations across more than 130 nations.
Directly connects to over 1,400 commercial telecommunication carriers and Internet service providers.
Delivers and defends up to 30% of daily global enterprise web traffic and media streaming.

name: Alibaba Cloud Global Backbone
famous_for: Global private enterprise network linking China's hyperscale computing hubs with Europe, APAC, and the Americas
story: Alibaba Cloud operates China's largest cloud infrastructure network, spanning dozens of regions worldwide connected by private high-speed terrestrial fiber and international subsea cables. Anchored in domestic hubs including Hangzhou, Beijing, Shanghai, and Zhangbei, the backbone extends across trans-Pacific and Eurasian routes to Frankfurt, London, Singapore, Tokyo, and Silicon Valley. Using its Cloud Enterprise Network (CEN) technology, enterprise customers establish automated cross-border connections compliant with international telecommunications frameworks.

Anchored in domestic green compute hubs including Zhangbei (Hebei) and Gui'an (Guizhou).

name: AWS Intercontinental Cloud Backbone
famous_for: Global private fiber network interconnecting AWS regions across continents on redundant 100GbE and 400GbE paths
story: Amazon Web Services operates a purpose-built global network backbone connecting cloud regions across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Oceania. Inter-region traffic stays on Amazon's private fiber infrastructure rather than the public Internet, encrypting automatically across all trans-oceanic and terrestrial links. Anchored by hyperscale clusters in Northern Virginia, Oregon, Dublin, Frankfurt, Tokyo, Singapore, Sydney, and São Paulo, the network utilizes redundant 100 Gbps and 400 Gbps wavelength paths over consortium cables and private dark fiber.

Operates dedicated trans-oceanic cables including investments in Hawaiki, Jupiter, and trans-Atlantic capacity.

name: Bifrost Submarine Cable System
famous_for: First direct subsea cable connecting Singapore to North America via the Java Sea and Celebes Sea bypassing Taiwan
story: Bifrost is a groundbreaking 15,000-kilometer trans-Pacific subsea cable developed by Meta, Keppel Telecommunications & Transportation, and Telin (Indonesia). Unlike historical routes that routed north via Japan and the Luzon Strait, Bifrost charts a unique southern trajectory through the Java Sea, Celebes Sea, and south of the Philippines across Guam to southern California and Oregon. Built with high-capacity space-division multiplexing fiber, Bifrost delivers massive direct bandwidth between Southeast Asia and Silicon Valley while avoiding seismically vulnerable straits.
notable: Pioneers a direct trans-Pacific route connecting Singapore and Jakarta straight to the US West Coast.
Spans over 15,000 kilometers crossing the Java Sea, Celebes Sea, and Pacific via Guam.
Delivers up to 10.4 Tbps per fiber pair across multiple high-density fiber pairs.
Significantly reduces trans-Pacific latency while circumventing earthquake-prone waters around Taiwan and Luzon.

famous_for: China's national compute grid channeling massive eastern AI & data workloads to western renewable energy hubs
story: China's 'Eastern Data, Western Computing' (东数西算) mega-project was formally launched in 2022 by the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) to balance national computing demands with green energy distribution. The infrastructure connects four eastern demand epicenters (Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Yangtze River Delta, Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao, and Chengdu-Chongqing) with four western renewable energy resource basins: Guizhou, Inner Mongolia, Gansu (Qingyang), and Ningxia (Zhongwei). Dedicated ultra-low-latency direct optical expressways ensure cross-country latencies remain under 20 ms.

Channels high-throughput AI model training and data processing to windy, solar-rich western provinces.
Constructs direct optical cross-connects maintaining inter-hub latencies under 20 milliseconds across thousands of kilometers.

name: Cloudflare Global Anycast Edge Network
famous_for: Global Anycast edge network spanning 330+ cities across 120+ countries delivering security and CDN
story: Cloudflare protects and accelerates Internet applications through a software-defined architecture that runs identical server stacks across every single edge point of presence. By advertising IP prefixes via BGP Anycast from every location simultaneously, requests automatically terminate at the physically and topologically nearest data center. Spanning 330 cities in over 120 nations and directly interconnecting with more than 13,000 corporate networks and Internet exchanges, Cloudflare sits within 50 ms of approximately 95 percent of the world's connected population.
notable: Employs BGP Anycast routing so every edge data center advertises identical IP ranges across all continents.
Positioned within 50 milliseconds of approximately 95% of the world's connected population.

name: Curie Submarine Cable
famous_for: Google's private 7,300 km subsea cable linking California directly to Valparaíso, Chile with a branch to Panama
story: Curie was Google's first private international subsea cable entirely financed and built by an American technology company. Spanning 7,300 kilometers from Los Angeles (landing at Equinix LA4 in El Segundo) down the Pacific coastline to Valparaíso, Chile, the four-fiber-pair system went live in 2019. Named after renowned physicist Marie Curie, it provides 72 Tbps of dedicated bandwidth directly interconnecting Google's North American network with its massive Latin American data center campus in Quilicura near Santiago.
notable: First private intercontinental subsea cable entirely funded by a non-telecom tech company.
Stretches 7,300 kilometers through deep eastern Pacific trenches from California to central Chile.

story: Founded in 1995 in Frankfurt am Main, DE-CIX grew into the world's highest-volume Internet Exchange, peaking at over 17 terabits per second in Frankfurt alone. Through GlobePEER, DE-CIX interconnects carrier-neutral exchange platforms across Europe, the United States, the Mediterranean, India, and Southeast Asia. Participants in New York, Dallas, Madrid, Marseille, Mumbai, and Singapore peer directly with European networks over an automated private software-defined interconnection overlay.

Interconnects dozens of metro exchanges across Europe, North America, India, and Southeast Asia.

name: Equiano
famous_for: Google's Portugal to South Africa cable, the first to switch capacity per fibre pair and the first to reach St Helena
story: Google announced Equiano in 2019 as a cable it would fund alone, to improve connectivity, resilience and latency for people in Africa. The trunk runs about 15,000 km from Sesimbra, Portugal, to Melkbosstrand near Cape Town, with branches to Lomé, Lagos, Swakopmund and St Helena. It was the first subsea cable to switch capacity per fibre pair instead of per wavelength, so whole pairs can be handed to partners such as WIOCC and Openserve. St Helena, which had relied on satellite, owns its 1,154 km branch; when service started in October 2023, measured latency from London fell from 657 ms to 131 ms.
notable: First subsea cable built to switch optically at the fibre-pair level rather than per wavelength, which Google said makes it simpler to add and reallocate capacity between locations.
Design capacity is 144 Tbps over 12 fibre pairs of 12 Tbps each; Google put it at about 20 times the capacity of the last cable built to serve the region.
St Helena's 1,154 km branch came ashore at Ruperts on 29 August 2021, the first shore landing of the whole Equiano project.
When St Helena went live on 1 October 2023, Kentik measured latency from London falling from 657 ms to 131 ms.
The trunk was announced with nine branching points off West Africa; at that time only a Lagos, Nigeria branch had a planned landing.

story: Equinix Fabric (formerly Equinix Cloud Exchange Fabric) links more than 260 International Business Exchange (IBX) data centers in dozens of metros across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East. Through automated software-defined networking, enterprises and service providers provision dedicated, jitter-free Layer 2 and Layer 3 connections between disparate clouds, financial trading desks, and network carriers within minutes rather than weeks. name: ESnet6 — US Department of Energy Science Network
operator: US Department of Energy / Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
famous_for: Multi-terabit scientific research backbone interconnecting Frontier, Aurora, El Capitan, and US national laboratories
story: The Energy Sciences Network (ESnet6) is the Department of Energy's dedicated high-performance scientific network. Managed by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, it interconnects all 17 DOE national laboratories, user facilities, and the nation's exascale supercomputers (Frontier at Oak Ridge, Aurora at Argonne, and El Capitan at Lawrence Livermore). Operating over a dedicated 15,000-mile nationwide optical fiber footprint with 400G and 800G optical channels, ESnet6 transfers petabytes of raw observational and computational physics data daily without touching commercial Internet routes.
notable: Transfers over 1.2 exabytes of scientific data annually across DOE's research and supercomputing complexes.
Connects all US exascale computing facilities: Frontier (ORNL), Aurora (ANL), and El Capitan (LLNL).

story: The European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) pools European Union and member-state resources to construct a world-leading supercomputing infrastructure. Interconnected over GÉANT's pan-European terabit-speed research backbone, the network joins world-class supercomputers including LUMI (Kajaani, Finland), Leonardo (Bologna, Italy), MareNostrum 5 (Barcelona, Spain), JUPITER (Jülich, Germany), MeluXina (Luxembourg), and Karolina (Czech Republic). The high-speed research mesh enables trans-European distributed workflows in fusion energy, climate modeling, and large foundation AI training.

name: Fidelity Investments Dual-Core Enterprise DR Pair
famous_for: Synchronous disaster recovery pair linking primary financial systems across Merrimack NH and Smithfield RI
story: Fidelity Investments operates one of Wall Street's benchmark enterprise disaster recovery pairs to safeguard trillions of dollars in customer assets. Engineered under strict post-9/11 financial continuity guidelines, the enterprise topology pairs two multi-megawatt tier-class enterprise campuses in Merrimack, New Hampshire and Smithfield, Rhode Island. Separated by approximately 75 miles (120 km) — outside the same regional power grid failure zone yet within the latency threshold for zero-data-loss synchronous database mirroring — the sites operate in continuous active-active load sharing with sub-millisecond heartbeat failover.
notable: Engineered to meet SEC and Federal Reserve interagency financial business continuity guidelines.
Distance of ~75 miles satisfies synchronous replication optical physics (sub-2 ms round trip fiber latency).

name: Google Dunant Submarine Cable
famous_for: Google's private 250 Tbps trans-Atlantic cable featuring 12 fiber pairs and space-division multiplexing
story: Dunant was Google's first private trans-Atlantic subsea cable, linking Virginia Beach in the United States directly to Saint-Hilaire-de-Riez on the Atlantic coast of France. Named after Red Cross founder Henry Dunant, the 6,400 km system went live in 2020 with 12 fiber pairs operating space-division multiplexing (SDM) from SubCom. With a design capacity of 250 Tbps, Dunant delivers high-throughput, low-latency interconnection between Google Cloud mega-campuses in North America and Western Europe without reliance on consortium consortium arrangements.

story: Google's internal inter-datacenter WAN, known historically as B4, revolutionized computer networking by proving Software-Defined Networking (SDN) at planetary scale using custom OpenFlow switches and centralized traffic engineering. Running over thousands of route-kilometers of private terrestrial dark fiber and trans-oceanic cables—including Curie, Dunant, Grace Hopper, and Unity—it connects hyperscale server farms across North America, Europe, Asia, and South America to power Search, YouTube, Workspace, and Google Cloud Platform services.

story: Grace Hopper is a private subsea cable system built by Google connecting Bellport, New York to Bude in the United Kingdom and Sopelana/Bilbao in Spain. Spanning over 6,200 km, it incorporates 16 fiber pairs with a combined design capacity of approximately 352 Tbps. It was Google's first direct cable investment landing in Spain and was the first subsea cable worldwide to deploy optical switching technology at the fiber level, allowing automated traffic rerouting around physical link interruptions.

story: Oracle redesigned its cloud infrastructure with Gen 2 OCI, implementing a strictly non-blocking flat network architecture that avoids oversubscribed packet routing between data centers. story: The Pakistan & East Africa Connecting Europe (PEACE) Cable is a 15,000-kilometer private subsea cable system engineered to provide the shortest geodetic transit route between China/Pakistan and Europe. Originating in Gwadar and Karachi, the network crosses the Arabian Sea to Djibouti and Mombasa, before traversing Egypt overland to terminate in Marseille, France. Financed by Chinese communications equipment vendor Hengtong Optic-Electric and operated as an open-access carrier-neutral system, PEACE delivers up to 96 Tbps across its Mediterranean and Indian Ocean segments.

story: The Southeast Asia–Middle East–Western Europe 6 (SEA-ME-WE 6) cable system is a high-capacity optical highway spanning 21,700 kilometers across two oceans and three continents. name: Spread Networks Chicago-to-New Jersey Financial Route
famous_for: Direct 825-mile dark-fiber route blasted through the Appalachians, cutting Chicago–NJ latency to sub-13 ms
story: Completed in 2010 at a cost of $300 million, Spread Networks' 825-mile underground fiber route was built in near-perfect straight lines, tunneling through the Allegheny and Appalachian mountains rather than following winding rail corridors or highways. The line directly connected the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) in Aurora, Illinois to the equity matching engines in Secaucus and Carteret, New Jersey. By shaving round-trip transmission time from 16.5 ms down to 12.98 ms, it ignited the modern algorithmic high-frequency trading (HFT) revolution documented in Michael Lewis's book 'Flash Boys'.
notable: Constructed in total secrecy between 2008 and 2010 with $300M in private funding.
